# Overview

`landisR` is a standalone R/Rcpp implementation of the living-biomass
succession processes validated against LANDIS-II Biomass Succession.

LANDIS-II is optional. A `landisR` project can be created in three ways:

```text
LANDIS-II inputs ---- landis_read() -----------\
R-native tables ----- landis_build() ------------> landisR_project -> landis_run()
canonical inputs ---- landis_from_canonical() ---/
```

All three routes converge to the same canonical project representation before
the scientific engine is called.

The beta.2 scientific scope includes living biomass, Ward seed dispersal,
stochastic establishment, compact RDS outputs, and direct comparison with
LANDIS-II outputs.

Dead biomass pools are outside the validated beta scope.

# Installation

Install the source package with:

```{r install}
install.packages(
  "landisR_0.1.0.9002.tar.gz",
  repos = NULL,
  type = "source"
)
```

Then load it:

```{r load}
library(landisR)
```

On Windows, installing from source requires a working Rtools toolchain because
the package contains compiled C++ code.

# Creating a project

## Route 1: existing LANDIS-II project

If you already have a LANDIS-II scenario, use `landis_read()`:

```{r landis-read}
project <- landis_read(
  "D:/LANDIS/my_project",
  scenario = "scenario.txt"
)

print(project)
```

`landis_read()` does not run LANDIS-II. It parses the supported LANDIS-II input
files and converts them to the native `landisR` canonical representation.

This route is useful when you want to:

- reproduce an existing LANDIS-II Biomass Succession scenario in `landisR`;
- compare `landisR` and LANDIS-II outputs;
- migrate an existing project toward a more flexible R workflow.

## Route 2: R-native inputs

LANDIS-II files are not required. A project can be built directly from R
objects:

```{r landis-build}
project <- landis_build(
  landscape = landscape,
  species = species,
  species_parameters = species_parameters,
  ecoregions = ecoregions,
  ecoregion_parameters = ecoregion_parameters,
  dynamic = dynamic,
  initial_cohorts = initial_cohorts,
  shade = shade,
  light = light,
  fire_reductions = fire_reductions,
  duration = 300,
  cell_length = 250,
  timestep = 10,
  initial_mode = "explicit_biomass",
  name = "experimental_landscape"
)
```

This route is intended for:

- synthetic landscapes;
- experimental designs;
- inputs generated from GIS workflows;
- outputs from other ecological models;
- future coupling with disturbance or management models;
- projects that have never been processed by LANDIS-II.

For the exact validated column names and R classes, see
`INPUT_SCHEMA_VALIDATED_5KM.md` in the installed package documentation.

## Route 3: canonical inputs

An existing canonical landisR project can be loaded directly:

```{r canonical}
project <- landis_from_canonical(
  "inputs_R/my_project",
  name = "my_project"
)
```

Advanced users can also provide an already prepared canonical R list.

# Required R-native inputs

The most important input tables are summarized below.

## Landscape

The landscape table must contain the complete rectangular grid, including
inactive cells.

Required columns are:

```text
cell_id
row
col
ecoregion_map_code
ecoregion
active
community
```

The validated indexing rule is:

```{r cell-id}
cell_id <- row + (col - 1L) * nrow
```

Active cells must reference a known ecoregion and a valid initial community.
Inactive cells use `community = 0`.

## Initial cohorts

For the validated `explicit_biomass` route:

```text
map_code
species
age
biomass
```

Each `(map_code, species, age)` combination must be unique.

Age must be at least 1 year and biomass must be finite and non-negative.

## Dynamic succession parameters

The dynamic table uses:

```text
year
ecoregion
species
sep
max_anpp
max_biomass
```

Each `(year, ecoregion, species)` combination must be unique.

`sep` is the establishment parameter. In the validated beta input validator it
must be between 0 and 1.

## Other ecological tables

`landis_build()` also requires:

```text
species
species_parameters
ecoregions
ecoregion_parameters
shade
light
fire_reductions
```

The exact current schemas are documented in
`INPUT_SCHEMA_VALIDATED_5KM.md`, which is generated directly from the
scientifically validated 5 x 5 km reference rather than copied manually.

# Running a simulation

A simulation is started with `landis_run()`:

```{r run}
sim <- landis_run(
  project = project,
  duration = 30,
  seed = 4357,
  output_directory = "outputs/my_run"
)

print(sim)
```

You can select output years explicitly:

```{r output-years}
sim <- landis_run(
  project = project,
  duration = 30,
  seed = 4357,
  output_years = c(0, 10, 20, 30),
  output_directory = "outputs/my_run"
)
```

The validated public beta uses:

```{r ward}
sim <- landis_run(
  project = project,
  duration = 30,
  seed = 4357,
  dispersal = "ward",
  ward_variant = "ward2019",
  output_directory = "outputs/my_run"
)
```

# Outputs

The native production format is compact RDS output rather than GeoTIFF.

A typical run contains:

```text
outputs/my_run/
  snapshots/
    snapshot_000.rds
    snapshot_010.rds
    ...
  checkpoints/
    ...
  biomass_summary.csv
  performance_profile.csv
```

A compact snapshot stores the state of active cells using state compression,
including species biomass, total biomass, maximum age, and ecoregion context.

This design avoids the large I/O cost of writing many TIFF files during every
simulation. Raster export can be done later as a post-processing step when
needed.

# Climate-sensitive inputs

Dynamic parameters can vary by year, ecoregion, and species.

A project can use the dynamic table already stored in its inputs:

```{r baseline}
sim <- landis_run(
  project,
  duration = 130,
  seed = 4357,
  output_directory = "outputs/baseline"
)
```

The public API also exposes a climate configuration argument for workflows that
replace the dynamic parameter table.

Climate tables should preserve the same canonical schema and cover all required
species and active ecoregions for the requested simulation period.

# Comparing with LANDIS-II

If an equivalent LANDIS-II simulation already exists, use `landis_compare()`:

```{r compare}
comparison <- landis_compare(
  run = sim,
  landis_outputs = "D:/LANDIS/reference_run",
  project = project,
  years = c(0, 10, 20, 30)
)

print(comparison)
```

The comparison can evaluate:

- biomass by species;
- `TotalBiomass`;
- `AGE-MAX`;
- cell-level differences;
- spatial correlation.

LANDIS-II validation TIFFs may be vertically mirrored and may not contain useful
georeferencing. With `orientation = "auto"`, `landis_compare()` tests the
year-zero state and selects the orientation that reproduces the initial state
exactly.

The optional package `terra` is required for this comparison workflow.

# Random seeds and stochastic equivalence

`landisR` uses its own R random-number stream.

A numeric seed such as:

```{r seed}
seed <- 4357
```

makes a `landisR` run reproducible, but the same numeric seed in LANDIS-II does
not imply the same random-number sequence across the two software engines.

For this reason:

- deterministic processes were validated by disabling recruitment and requiring
  exact cell-level equality;
- stochastic recruitment was validated using distributions from 20 independent
  replicates in each engine.

The beta validation supports stochastic equivalence at the ensemble level.

# Scientific validation of beta.2

The deterministic external validation against LANDIS-II used a 5 x 5 km
landscape with 396 active cells.

Recruitment was disabled by setting SEP to zero in both engines.

The result was:

```text
76 / 76 comparisons EXACT
```

This included 17 species, `TotalBiomass`, and `AGE-MAX` at years 0, 10, 20,
and 30.

The stochastic ensemble validation used 20 independent replicates in each
engine.

Summary:

```text
Initial state              380 / 380 EXACT
Species SMD                 51 / 51 within diagnostic band
Species occupancy           51 / 51 within diagnostic band
Spatial structure           51 / 51 within diagnostic band
Brown-Forsythe p < 0.05      0 / 51
Brown-Forsythe BH < 0.05     0 / 51
TotalBiomass                PASS at all evaluated years
AGE-MAX                     EXACT
```

The installable R package also reproduced the validated development beta
exactly in the package smoke test.

# Current beta scope

The following functionality is part of the validated beta scope:

```text
living biomass
explicit initial biomass
Ward 2019 seed dispersal
stochastic establishment
climate-sensitive dynamic parameters
compact RDS snapshots/checkpoints
LANDIS-II input adapter
R-native input construction
LANDIS-II output comparison
no internal parallelism
```

The following are not yet part of the validated public beta:

```text
dead biomass pools
public disturbance-extension API
fully validated age-spinup workflow
automatic GeoTIFF production during simulation
```

The source code may contain historical development pathways related to some of
these features, but they should not be interpreted as supported public API.

# Reproducible project structure

A practical research project can be organized as:

```text
my_project/
  inputs/
  scripts/
  outputs/
  comparisons/
```

For LANDIS-independent workflows, the input tables can be generated entirely in
R and saved with `landis_write_canonical()`:

```{r write-canonical}
landis_write_canonical(
  project,
  "inputs/canonical",
  overwrite = TRUE
)
```

The canonical representation can then be reused for multiple simulations and
climate scenarios.

# Finding the complete documentation

After installation:

```{r docs}
system.file(
  "doc",
  package = "landisR"
)
```

The package documentation includes:

```text
QUICK_START.md
INPUTS.md
INPUT_SCHEMA_VALIDATED_5KM.md
FUNCTION_REFERENCE.md
VALIDATION.md
```

The main R help pages are:

```{r help}
?landisR
?landis_read
?landis_run
?landis_compare
```

The public API intentionally remains small. Functions beginning with `bs52_`
are internal implementation details and are not part of the supported user
interface.
